verses.zh: （亚萨的诗歌。）　神啊，求你不要静默！　神啊，求你不要闭口，也不要不作声！
verses.en: A song, a psalm of Asaph.O God, do not be silent.Do not ignore us.[NOTE:1] Do not be inactive, O God.
notes: Psalm 83. The psalmist asks God to deliver Israel from the attacks of foreign nations. Recalling how God defeated Israel’s enemies in the days of Deborah and Gideon, he prays that the hostile nations would be humiliated.
verses.commentary:
83:1-8 This strophe describes the inappropriate activities of the surrounding
nations. The psalmist requests that God act on Israel's behalf.

- do not remain quiet ‒ BDB 198, no VERB but parallel to #2, #3

- do not be silent ‒ BDB 361, KB 357, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense, cf. Ps. 28:1; 35:22; 50:3; 109:1

- do not be still (i.e., inactive) ‒ BDB 1052, KB 1641, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

The fact that the surrounding nations planned and acted out their aggression
(Ps. 83:2-8) caused the covenant people to wonder at YHWH's apparent inactivity.

Notice the activity of the surrounding nations.

- make un uproar ‒ BDB 242, KB 250, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 46:6 and very similar to Ps. 2:1-2

- exalted themselves (lit. raised their heads) ‒ BDB 669, KB 724, Qal PERFECT, cf. Jdgs. 8:28; Zech. 1:21

- made shrewd plans ‒ BDB 791, KB 886, Hiphil IMPERFECT, only here in Hiphil in the OT

- conspire together ‒ BDB 419, KB 421, Hithpael IMPERFECT, used in the
sense of "determine" in 2 Chr. 30:23

- come ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE

- wipe them out ‒ BDB 470, KB 469, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a
COHORTATIVE sense, cf. Ps. 74:8

- that the name of Israel be remembered no more ‒ BDB 269, KB 269, Niphal IMPERFECT,
which is an idiom for total destruction and death

The conclusion to this list is stated in Ps. 83:5. An attack on Israel is an attack on YHWH, cf. Ps. 83:2; Ps. 2:2; 74:18,23.

verses.zh: 因为你的仇敌喧嚷，恨你的抬起头来。
verses.en: For look, your enemies are making a commotion;those who hate you are hostile.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “do not be deaf.”

verses.zh: 他们同谋奸诈要害你的百姓，彼此商议要害你所隐藏的人。
verses.en: They carefully plot[NOTE:1] against your people,and make plans to harm[NOTE:2] the ones you cherish.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “lift up [their] head[s].” The phrase “lift up [the] head” here means “to threaten; to be hostile,” as in Judg 8:28.
Heb “they make crafty a plot.”
Heb “and consult together against.”
verses.commentary:
83:3 "Your people. . .Your treasured ones" The second expression (BDB 860, KB 1049, Qal
PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, means both "to hide" and "to hide as a treasure") has two possible connotations in BDB.

- treasured (JPSOA), cf. Exod. 19:5; Deut. 7:6; 14:2; 26:18

- hidden with God, cf. Ps. 27:5; 31:21

The NKJV has "sheltered ones" (#2), while NJB has "those you cherish" (#1).

verses.zh: 他们说：来吧，我们将他们剪灭，使他们不再成国！使以色列的名不再被人记念！
verses.en: They say, “Come on, let’s annihilate them so they are no longer a nation.[NOTE:1] Then the name of Israel will be remembered no more.”
notes: The passive participle of the Hebrew verb צָפַן (tsafan, “to hide”) is used here in the sense of “treasured; cherished.”
verses.commentary:
83:4 This is the main problem. These surrounding nations did not recognize God's
purpose involving Israel. Israel was meant to be a light to the nations, but the nations wanted
to put out that light (God's light) permanently.

This is exactly what Satan tries to do in Genesis.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATANIC ATTEMPTS TO THWART THE MESSIANIC LINE IN GENESIS

▣ "the name of Israel" This is a way of referring to the nation (cf. Ps. 83:4a).

For the meaning of the name "Israel" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the Name).

verses.zh: 他们同心商议，彼此结盟，要抵挡你，
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] they devise a unified strategy;[NOTE:2] they form an alliance[NOTE:3] against you.
notes: Heb “we will cause them to disappear from [being] a nation.”
Or “for.”
Heb “they consult [with] a heart together.”
verses.commentary: 83:5 "covenant" Covenant here refers to the nations' plans to annihilate Israel.

verses.zh: 就是住帐棚的以东人和以实玛利人，摩押和夏甲人，
verses.en: It includes[NOTE:1] the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,Moab and the Hagrites,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “cut a covenant.”
The words “it includes” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
83:6 "tents of. . ." This is an idiomatic anachronism of when Israel lived in "tents," but at
this period most of them lived in cities and villages with more permanent housing.

The other possibility is that it is idiomatic for a nation (cf. Ps. 120:5).

▣ "Edom" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDOM AND ISRAEL

▣ "Ishmaelites" This refers to the descendants of Ishmael, Abraham's
first child by Hagar (cf. Gen. 25:12-16). They became the Arab tribes. It is used in

- an ethnic sense

- a commercial sense of traveling traders

▣ "Moab" This is one of the two nations descended from Lot
and his daughters (cf. Gen. 19:30-38). They were relatives of Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOAB

▣ "Hagrites" This is a tribe from Ishmael mentioned in 1 Chr. 5:10,18-22.
The name may come from "Hagar," Ishmael's Egyptian mother. They lived to the east of
Canaan and some parts of the tribe, more to the southeast.

verses.zh: 迦巴勒、亚扪，和亚玛力、非利士并泰尔的居民。
verses.en: Gebal,[NOTE:1] Ammon, and Amalek,Philistia, and the inhabitants of Tyre.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hagrites are also mentioned in 1 Chr 5:10, 19-20.

Some identify Gebal with the Phoenician coastal city of Byblos (see Ezek 27:9, where the name is spelled differently), though others locate this site south of the Dead Sea (see BDB 148 s.v. גְּבַל; HALOT 174 s.v. גְּבַל).
verses.commentary:
83:7 "Gebal" This name (BDB 148, KB 174) can have two possible references.

- from the word for "mountain," may refer to an area in the trans-Jordan area near
Petra, thereby connected to Arab tribe

- from the name of an old Phoenician coastal city and, therefore, would parallel Tyre
(cf. Ezek. 27:9), later known as Byblos

▣ "Ammon" See notes on Moab, Ps. 83:6.

SPECIAL TOPIC: AMMON

▣ "Amalek" A descendant of Esau, who
became chief in Edom (cf. Gen. 36:15-16). They were especially problematic to
Israel during the wilderness wandering period (cf. Exod. 17:8-16; Num. 24:20;
Deut. 25:12-19. Saul was commanded to destroy them (cf. 1 Samuel 15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: AMALEK

▣ "Philistia" The Philistines were apparently Greeks from the
Aegean Islands. They were the only group of people in this part of the world who
were uncircumcized. They were apparently a mercenary force who tried to attack
Egypt in the twelfth century B.C. but were defeated. They then settled
on the southern coast of Palestine. They had five major cities which are delineated
in Josh.13:3: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron. They were a major military
problem throughout the period of the judges and even throughout the reign of Saul and
David. The name "Palestine" comes from the word "Philistine."

SPECIAL TOPIC: PHILISTINES

▣ "Tyre" This is the famous seaport of
the Phoenician Empire north of Israel. The older capital was "Sidon" (and
possibly older than that, Gebal).

verses.zh: 亚述也与他们连合；他们作罗得子孙的帮手。（细拉）
verses.en: Even Assyria has allied with them,lending its strength to the descendants of Lot.[NOTE:1] (Selah)
notes: For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
verses.commentary:
83:8 "Assyria" This was a major empire of
the Tigris/Euphrates. It became powerful in about the middle 900's B.C. to
609 B.C., when the capital of Nineveh fell (Nahum).

The mentioning of Assyria and not Babylon is a hint of the date
this Psalm was written.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA

▣ The Assyrians had become a help
(lit. "arm") for the trans-Jordan nations that descended from Lot and his two
daughters (cf. Gen. 19:30-38).

- Moab

- Ammon

▣ "Selah" See notes at Psalm 3:2.

verses.zh: 求你待他们，如待米甸，如在基顺河待西西拉和耶宾一样。
verses.en: Do to them as you did to Midian[NOTE:1]—as you did to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River.[NOTE:2]
notes: The descendants of Lot were the Moabites and Ammonites.tn Heb “they are an arm for the sons of Lot.” The “arm” is here a symbol of military might.
Heb “do to them like Midian.”
verses.commentary:
83:9-12 This strophe reminds the
current Israelites of YHWH's presence and help in the past when invaders plotted
to take Israel's land.

- as with Midian ‒ Jdgs. 7:22

- Sisera and Jabin ‒ Jdgs. 4:22-23

- Oreb and Zeeb ‒ Jdgs. 7:25

- Zebah and Zalmunna ‒ Jdgs. 8:21

83:9-11 (i.e., Judges 4-8). The UBS Text Project (p. 341) gives En-dor an "A"
rating and rejects the emendation. Though not mentioned by name, it is still in
the general area (cf. Josh. 17:11).

verses.zh: 他们在隐・多珥灭亡，成了地上的粪土。
verses.en: They were destroyed at Endor;[NOTE:1] their corpses were like manure[NOTE:2] on the ground.
notes: The psalmist alludes here to Gideon’s victory over the Midianites (see Judg 7-8) and to Barak’s victory over Jabin’s army, which was led by his general Sisera (Judg 4-5).

Endor is not mentioned in the accounts of Gideon’s or Barak’s victories, but both battles took place in the general vicinity of the town. (See Y. Aharoni and M. Avi-Yonah, The Macmillan Bible Atlas, 46, 54.) Because Sisera and Jabin are mentioned in v. 9b, many understand them to be the subject of the verbs in v. 10, though they relate v. 10 to Gideon’s victory, which is referred to in v. 9a, 11. (See, for example, Y. Aharoni, The Land of the Bible, 263.)
verses.commentary:
83:10 "as dung for the ground" This imagery refers to the huge number
of dead bodies after a battle. The prospect of being improperly buried or eaten by
animals would terrify ANE people (cf. 2 Kgs. 9:37; Ps. 79:2-3; Jer. 8:2; 16:4; 25:33;
36:30). This was a curse formula!

▣ "En-dor" This location is mentioned
in Saul's day but not in the book of Judges. The NEB changes it to En-harod,
which is mentioned in Jdgs. 7:1 and fits with the historical allusions of Ps.

verses.zh: 求你叫他们的首领像俄立和西伊伯，叫他们的王子都像西巴和撒慕拿。
verses.en: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb,[NOTE:1] and all their rulers like Zebah and Zalmunna,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they were manure.” In addition to this passage, corpses are compared to manure in 2 Kgs 9:37; Jer 8:2; 9:21; 16:4; 25:33.
Oreb and Zeeb were the generals of the Midianite army that was defeated by Gideon. The Ephraimites captured and executed both of them and sent their heads to Gideon (Judg 7:24-25).
verses.commentary:
83:11 There are two allusions to God's past victories.

- "Oreb and Zeeb" were Midianite generals defeated and beheaded by
the tribe of Ephraim at Gideon's request, Jdgs. 7:24-25

- "Zebah and Zalmunna" were Midianite kings killed by Gideon, Jdgs. 8:18-21

verses.zh: 他们说：我们要得　神的住处，作为自己的产业。
verses.en: who said,[NOTE:1] “Let’s take over[NOTE:2] the pastures of God.”
notes: Zebah and Zalmunna were the Midianite kings. Gideon captured them and executed them (Judg 8:1-21).

The translation assumes that “Zebah and Zalmunna” are the antecedents of the relative pronoun (“who [said]”). Another option is to take “their nobles…all their rulers” as the antecedent and to translate, “those who say.”

verses.zh: 我的　神啊，求你叫他们像旋风的尘土，像风前的碎秸。
verses.en: O my God, make them like dead thistles,[NOTE:1] like dead weeds blown away by[NOTE:2] the wind.
notes: Heb “let’s take possession for ourselves.”

Or “tumbleweed.” The Hebrew noun גַּלְגַּל (galgal) refers to a “wheel” or, metaphorically, to a whirling wind (see Ps 77:18). If taken in the latter sense here, one could understand the term as a metonymical reference to dust blown by a whirlwind (cf. NRSV “like whirling dust”). However, HALOT 190 s.v. II גַּלְגַּל understands the noun as a homonym referring to a “dead thistle” here and in Isa 17:13. The parallel line, which refers to קַשׁ (qash, “chaff”), favors this interpretation.
verses.commentary:
83:13-18 This strophe is a prayer for
YHWH to act in judgment on Israel's behalf.

- make them ‒ BDB 1011, KB 1483, Qal IMPERATIVE

- like whirling dust, cf. Isa. 17:13; 29:5; 41:15-16

- like chaff before the wind, cf. Isa. 17:13

- like fire that burns the forest

- like a flame that sets the mountains on fire

- pursue them ‒ BDB 922, KB 1191, Qal IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense

- terrify them ‒ BDB 96, KB 111, Piel IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- fill their faces with dishonor ‒ BDB 569, KB 583, Piel IMPERATIVE

- let them be ashamed ‒ BDB 101, KB 116, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- let them be dismayed ‒ BDB 96, KB 111, Niphal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- let them be humiliated ‒ BDB 344, KB 340, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- let them perish ‒ BDB 1, KB 2, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

There are two more which show the intended purpose of judgment, which is to
help the nations come to worship YHWH (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

- that they may seek Your name, O YHWH ‒ BDB134, KB 152, Piel
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense (Ps. 83:16)

- that they may know that You alone are the Most High over all the earth ‒
BDB 393, KB 390, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense (Ps. 83:18)

83:13 Notice the different terms used to describe God's judgment as a wind storm.
Remember, these are desert people.

- whirling dust, 83:13a (BDB 165, cf. Ps. 77:18)

- chaff before wind, 83:13b (cf. Isa. 17:13)

- tempest, 83:15a (BDB 704, cf. Jonah 1:4,12; Amos 1:14)

- Your storm, 83:15b (BDB 693 I, cf. Isa. 17:13; 21:1; 29:6; Hosea 8:2; Nahum 1:3)

verses.zh: 火怎样焚烧树林，火焰怎样烧着山岭，
verses.en: Like the fire that burns down the forest,or the flames that consume the mountainsides,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “before.”

verses.zh: 求你也照样用狂风追赶他们，用暴雨恐吓他们。
verses.en: chase them with your gale windsand terrify[NOTE:1] them with your windstorm.
notes: The imagery of fire and flames suggests unrelenting, destructive judgment.

verses.zh: 愿你使他们满面羞耻，好叫他们寻求你―耶和华的名！
verses.en: Cover[NOTE:1] their faces with shame,so they might seek[NOTE:2] you,[NOTE:3] O Lord.
notes: The two imperfect verbal forms in v. 15 express the psalmist’s wish or prayer.
Heb “fill.”
After the preceding imperative, the prefixed verbal form with prefixed vav (ו) indicates purpose or result (“then they will seek”).
verses.commentary:
83:16 "Your name, O Lord" The name stands for
the person.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

verses.zh: 愿他们永远羞愧惊惶！愿他们惭愧灭亡！
verses.en: May they be humiliated and continually terrified.[NOTE:1] May they die in shame.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your name,” which stands here for God’s person.

Heb “and may they be terrified to perpetuity.” The Hebrew expression עֲדֵי־עַד (ʿade ʿad, “to perpetuity”) can mean “forevermore” (see Pss 92:7; 132:12, 14), but here it may be used hyperbolically, for the psalmist asks that the experience of judgment might lead the nations to recognize (v. 18) and even to seek (v. 16) God.
verses.commentary:
83:17 Notice the parallelism between "forever" and "perish." These reflect on
Ps. 83:4, where the nations wanted Israel to cease to exist!

verses.zh: 使他们知道：惟独你―名为耶和华的―是全地以上的至高者！
verses.en: Then they will know[NOTE:1] that you alone are the Lord,[NOTE:2] the Most High[NOTE:3] over all the earth.
notes: Heb “may they be ashamed and perish.” The four prefixed verbal forms in this verse are understood as jussives. The psalmist concludes his prayer with an imprecation, calling severe judgment down on his enemies. The strong language of the imprecation seems to run contrary to the positive outcome of divine judgment envisioned in v. 16b. Perhaps the language of v. 17 is overstated for effect. Another option is that v. 16b expresses an ideal, while the strong imprecation of vv. 17-18 anticipates reality. It would be nice if the defeated nations actually pursued a relationship with God, but if judgment does not bring them to that point, the psalmist asks that they be annihilated so that they might at least be forced to acknowledge God’s power.
After the preceding jussives (v. 17), the prefixed verbal form with prefixed vav (ו) indicates purpose (“so that they may know”) or result.
Heb “that you, your name [is] the Lord, you alone.”
verses.commentary:
83:18 "over all the earth" This
universal element is common in the Psalms of Asaph! It is the obvious necessary
conclusion to monotheism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide
commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of
the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible and the
Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a
commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think
through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought provoking, not definitive.

- Does this Psalm reflect a historical invasion by a coalition of nations or historical imagery?

- How does Ps. 83:1 reflect the fear and confusion of Israel?

- How are Ps. 83:4-5 related to YHWH's larger redemptive plan? Is there a Satanic attempt
to thwart God's redemptive activity?

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in
the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one
and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- YHWH is intimately linked to His covenant people. The planning and scheming of
the surrounding ANE nations to attack Israel, is a plan to attack Him (cf. Ps. 83:5 and note Ps. 83:12).

- Several nations and people groups are mentioned.

- Edom

- Ishmaelites

- Moab

- Hagrites

- Gebal

- Ammon

- Amalek

- Philistia

- Tyre (i.e., Phoenicia)

- Assyria

- Midian (Numbers 11-14 refer to events in Israel's past where YHWH helped them)

- Sisera and Jabin

- Oreb and Zech

- Zebah and Zalmunna

- This Psalm of prayer (5 IMPERATIVES OF REQUEST) for the destruction of Israel's
enemies is characterized by a large number of IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense.

- Ps. 83:1 ‒ two stated but three implied

- Ps. 83:15-18 ‒ six (possibly eight with Ps. 83:15)

- This Psalm uses several names for Deity.

- God, Ps. 83:1a, 12b ‒ Elohim (BDB 43)

- God, Ps. 83:1b ‒ El (BDB 42)

- God, Ps. 83:13a ‒ Eloah (BDB 43)

- Lord, Ps. 83:16b, 18a ‒ YHWH (BDB 217)

- Most High, Ps. 83:18b ‒ Elyon (BDB 751)

See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY

- This Psalm has a strong

- evangelistic thrust (i.e., Ps. 83:16b, 18)

- universal focus (Ps. 83:18b)
